answer.rationale: With expiration in 14 days, no auto-renew, and the line at 94% with no buffer, the hard constraint is continuity; switching or qualifying a new primary/second source inside this window would add delivery risk even if it could help the 18% mandate later. Incumbent renewal is the only action that reliably protects scheduled deliveries now, but it likely misses near-term cost reduction because the incumbent has refused to reopen price. I would treat this as a short guarded bridge/renewal posture where possible, preserve benchmark leverage from memory_c4 for the next cycle, and avoid deferral because memory_c5 applies only to non-critical services that can continue month-to-month.
